# Top 20 batters by reliability rating (generated by src/09_top10_tables.py)

Ranks 1-10 in bold are the submission. Levels and shift are Impact per 100 balls (0 = average outcome for the same situation; positive = helps the team's win chances). Consistency = shrunk share of pressure matches with positive win probability added. Rank interval and top-10 share: 1,000 match resamples (src/07_reliability.py). Confidence: secure = top 10 in >= 80% of resamples, probable 50-80%, marginal < 50%. Pressure balls count all tiers; IPL pressure balls shows how many of them are IPL. First-innings pressure balls are mostly the new ball (overs 1-2 of a first innings are almost all flagged), so the chase-only pressure rank (same pressure level, chase balls only, rank among the 105 eligible) shows who also holds up when chasing. P / R = pressure / routine balls (plain stats on IPL + full-member T20Is).

Confidence in the top 10: 2 secure, 5 probable, 3 marginal. The order inside a band is the point estimate only. Places 9-10 against 11-12 (share of resamples in the top 10): #9 Shreyas Iyer 39%, #10 Josh Inglis 40%, #11 Andre Russell 40%, #12 Suryakumar Yadav 33%. The intervals hold the WP model, priors and shrinkage strengths fixed, so they understate the true uncertainty. High-variance picks (an eligibility count within 25% of its minimum, fewer than 75 IPL pressure balls, or >= 75% of pressure balls in one season): #1 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (87% of pressure balls in 2026); #3 Priyansh Arya (446 balls (min 400)); #6 Finn Allen (38 IPL pressure balls (flag below 75)).
